data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts with a checklist is more reliable in expectation, but genuine reliability is proven only when the panel exhibits lower error variance than the expert without elevated systematic error on configural, checklist-silent items.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the panel's residual error is systematically aligned with the checklist's known cue-omissions, the gain is compliance-tracking, not genuine reliability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's variance is low (high consistency across bootstrapped subsets of cases), the panel's variance-reduction advantage vanishes and panel is not more reliable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task is dominated by configural integration not decomposable into checklist items, the checklist bias exceeds expert variance and the panel is worse.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklist+panel and intuition+expert map onto a bias-variance tradeoff: aggregation reduces variance, but the checklist injects bias by compressing the cue-space. Panel>expert iff the variance reduction exceeds the checklist's bias. In a single evaluation, decomposing the total error reveals whether the panel's advantage is variance-driven (genuine) or merely bias-tracking (compliance that happens to match the oracle).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
